correction: The install and update secure harnesses were believed to be independent test programs that could each carry their own copy of shared assertion helpers. They cannot: the copies drift silently, and the drift is load-bearing. type2_only diverged to accept only `efi` in the update harness while bootc writes `uki`, and esp_cat was never copied at all, so the update leg could never pass on any composefs install while the install harness asserted the same properties and passed eleven seconds earlier. correction: The check-image-updates push rejection ('refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow .github/workflows/build-images.yml without workflows permission') was believed fixable by adding `workflows: write` to the job's permissions block. It is not: `workflows` is not a valid scope in the Actions `permissions:` schema, so adding it makes the entire workflow file invalid (startup_failure, killing BOTH jobs including the healthy sysext one), and GITHUB_TOKEN structurally can never be granted workflow-file push rights. The only fix is the already-wired WORKFLOW_PAT secret: a fine-grained PAT with contents+pull-requests+workflows read/write, consumed via `token: ${{ secrets.WORKFLOW_PAT || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`.
evidence: PR #652 (3ed85bd) added `workflows: write`; run 31381342652 = startup_failure 'invalid workflow file'; underlying failure run 31377866762 shows the git push rejection with GITHUB_TOKEN; reverted in PR #653 (2c2c4d0); gh secret list shows no WORKFLOW_PAT as of 2026-08-10
promoted_to: comment on the Create image dependency PR step in check-dependencies.yml

scope: shared systemd unit retirement / persistent /etc enablement
correction: Retiring a shipped unit from the image was believed safe because the enablement-manifest/preset pipeline drops dangling symlinks and dangling wants are tolerated. It is not safe when the unit's [Install] carried RequiredBy=: first-boot presets persisted .requires links in the /etc overlay upper on /var, and on the next update the dangling Requires= invalidates PID 1's very first transaction -- 'Failed to isolate default target' before any service runs or the journal persists, so no runtime cleanup can ever fire. Fresh installs (hence every CI boot test) first-boot the NEW image's presets and are immune, which is exactly why no harness caught it; only installs first-booted before the retirement break, on every subsequent update.
evidence: e08311f retired snow-linux-live-setup.service (RequiredBy=multi-user.target + display-manager.service); image 20260812205454 failed 3 counted boots on an enrolled snow-ab machine (UKI left at +0-3, A/B fallback to 20260811110127); systemd-analyze verify --root over the new slot with the machine's real merged /etc reproduced 'graphical.target: Failed to create graphical.target/start: Unit snow-linux-live-setup.service not found', and the same merged /etc verified clean against the old root; removing the two .requires links made the transaction valid
promoted_to: CLAUDE.md 'Never use RequiredBy='; docs/adr/0013-no-requiredby-enablement-prune-stale-requires.md; frostyard/core ADR-0030; check-required-by-guard.sh + etc-overlay-prune.sh

scope: shared/outformat/image/buildah-package.sh secure digest probe / GitHub hosted runners
correction: A per-profile secure-build failure pattern (cayo/snow failing, snowfield passing, same commit) was believed to be image- or dependency-related. It was a runner-image lottery: GitHub rolls runner images out gradually, so matrix jobs in ONE run land on different images. ubuntu24/20260810.271 (podman 4.9.3 -> 5.8.4) sets mount_program = fuse-overlayfs in storage.conf, making every container rootfs fuse-overlayfs even rootful; bootc 1.16.7 hardcodes its temp composefs repo at /var/tmp INSIDE the container (tempfile::tempdir_in, TMPDIR ignored), and composefs object writes use O_TMPFILE, which fuse-overlayfs does not support -> 'os error 95' in every storage-digest probe. Also learned: reverting mount_program mid-job does NOT restore kernel overlayfs (already-initialized graphroot keeps fuse-overlayfs), so the fix must live in our probe invocation: bind a host scratch dir over the container's /var/tmp.
evidence: run 31721199554 attempts 1+2: all failures on 20260810.271, all passes on 20260720.247; debug run 31730148778 on 20260810.271: bare probe fails os error 95, probe with -v host-dir:/var/tmp returns a clean digest, storage.conf edit still mounts fuse.fuse-overlayfs; bootc v1.16.7 crates/lib/src/bootc_composefs/digest.rs:28 tempdir_in("/var/tmp")

correction: A bootc status containing spec.bootOrder=rollback and status.rollbackQueued=true alongside a new staged deployment looked like broken update ordering. Those fields are separate bootloader-ordering state and may correctly coexist with a valid .status.staged deployment; do not clear or repair them merely because an update was staged. Judge updater success by registry-manifest-digest continuity between Podman .Digest and bootc's booted/staged imageDigest, never by rollbackQueued or Podman .Id.

promoted_to: docs/design/build-pipeline.md Base update services; docs/design/overview.md Bootc Update Staging

correction: Believed a package explicitly selected with pkg/trixie-backports would have its dependencies resolved from the normal trixie candidates. Two corrections from the first flurry builds: (1) apt never auto-selects a priority-100 backports version for a TRANSITIVE dependency, so any dep that exists in both suites and needs the backports version (hyprland's libxkbcommon0 >= 1.12.3 vs trixie 1.7.0) must be suffixed by hand, exactly like the kernel fragment's mesa closure; (2) the opposite drag also exists: apt's 3.0 solver resolves a backports package's dependencies PREFERRING same-archive versions, so xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland/trixie-backports pulled libpipewire 1.4.9~bpo and made the strictly same-versioned trixie pipewire family unsatisfiable - the whole pipewire family had to move to backports, each member explicitly.
evidence: mkosi flurry builds 2/3 failed with the libspa-0.2-modules (= 1.4.2-1) conflict; podman trixie apt simulation with the base image dpkg status reproduced it, constrained delta-minimization reduced it to {xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland/trixie-backports, pipewire-audio}, and suffixing the 11-package pipewire family resolved 934 packages cleanly.

correction: The base package list was believed to install only what it names plus real dependencies. network-manager-applet (present since the first commit) Depends 'policykit-1-gnome | polkit-1-auth-agent'; policykit-1-gnome was removed from Debian after bookworm, so on trixie apt silently satisfies the virtual polkit-1-auth-agent with an arbitrary full desktop provider — the entire Cinnamon desktop in real mkosi builds (cinnamon, cinnamon-session, muffin, nemo, cjs...), ukui-polkit plus a Qt5/GDAL/OpenCV stack (~161 packages) under the host's apt — in EVERY image built on base, cayo server included. The accident also leaked into the cayo /var outcome map (colord/upower/xkb/fontconfig entries existed only via the accidental closure) and snow's RemovePackages=nm-connection-editor was a partial workaround that force-removed a hard versioned Depends of the still-installed applet. When adding any package to base, check its Depends for virtual-package alternations whose first real alternative no longer exists in the target suite: apt-get -s -o Dir::State::status=/dev/null install <list> diffs make the closure visible without a build.

correction: Believed the pinned stable-v2 cosign plus CI's verify step guaranteed downstream key-verification of published images. Two corrections: (1) cosign v2.6.3-v2.6.5 regress `verify --key` on digests carrying GitHub provenance-attestation referrers (error: no matching attestations: expected key signature, not certificate); v2.6.2 is the last good v2 (bisected against ghcr.io/frostyard/cayo). (2) CI's verify step runs BEFORE the attest-build-provenance step attaches that referrer, so it structurally cannot catch a cosign version that only breaks on attested images - which is the state every downstream verifier (firn installer preflight, manual cosign verify) actually sees.

correction: StartLimitIntervalSec=0 did NOT fix the staged-update notify watcher failures -- it unmasked a second limiter. PathExists= is level-triggered and re-arms on every triggered-service exit; with a semaphore that persists until reboot by design this retrigger-loops until systemd's path TriggerLimit (200/2s) fails the .path unit with 'trigger-limit-hit'. Fix: PathModified= only (edge-triggered), plus a static wants link on the condition-gated service for login-while-pending.
evidence: Reproduced in QEMU flurry VM 2026-08-26: writing /run/snosi/update-staged mid-session failed bootc-update-notify.path with Result=trigger-limit-hit in <3s, ~200 service starts in the journal; first seen live as a fumon 'Failed unit detected' toast on the snosi-firn-test incus VM.

scope: sysext udev rules and kernel modules
correction: The repeated claim that a sysext's udev rules and modules-load entries 'take effect on the next boot unless manually applied' (CLAUDE.md Sunshine paragraph, docs/design/sysexts.md sunshine entry, voxtype mkosi.conf comment) was wrong: they take effect on NO boot. systemd-sysext.service declares only Before=sysinit.target with no ordering against systemd-udevd.service, udev wins in practice, and udev parses its rules once at daemon start and is never told to look again. OPTIONS+="static_node=" does not rescue it, because udev applies static-node permissions only at daemon startup -- exactly when the rule does not yet exist.
evidence: Live snow install (voxtype merged, rebooted): journalctl -b -o short-monotonic shows systemd-udevd.service started at 8.36s and systemd-sysext.service began merging at 9.24s; /dev/uinput was root:root 0600 despite the merged /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/80-uinput.rules; ydotoold exited 'failed to open uinput device: Permission denied' into start-limit-hit; voxtype silently used fallback_to_clipboard (transcribed, typed nothing). `udevadm control --reload` then `modprobe uinput` produced root:input 0660 and a working ydotoold immediately.
promoted_to: shared/sysext/tree (snosi-sysext-udev-reload.service + script) + voxtype/sunshine wiring + test/sysext-udev-reload-test.sh + CLAUDE.md + docs/design/sysexts.md 'udev Rules and Kernel Modules in Sysexts'

scope: shared/snow/tree plymouth-start drop-in, native boot smoke gate
correction: The recurring snow-only 'plymouth-start.service killed, signal=SEGV -> degraded -> promote-snow skipped' failure (issue #850; main runs 33230153367 and 33465852243) was NOT a snow image defect and NOT the documented multi-GPU/NULL-serial-terminal case. The exact failing candidate bytes (snow-ab_20260901032038, fetched from the same .candidate URL CI used) passed test/native-boot-smoke-test.sh 7/7 locally. The snow-vs-snowfield difference is kernel config, not image config: the profiles differ only by shared/kernel/{backports,surface}, and linux-image-amd64/trixie-backports 7.1.8+deb13-amd64 has CONFIG_FRAMEBUFFER_CONSOLE=y WITHOUT CONFIG_FRAMEBUFFER_CONSOLE_DEFERRED_TAKEOVER, so fbcon rebinds the VT layer the moment virtio_gpu's fbdev registers, measured at t+4.95s inside plymouth-start's 4.69-5.44s window and ~40ms after /dev/dri/card0 (which is all the existing 10-wait-drm.conf waited for). linux-image-surface 6.19.8-surface-3 sets DEFERRED_TAKEOVER=y and never binds fbcon during boot (/sys/class/vtconsole holds only vtcon0 dummy bind=1 at multi-user), so snowfield never enters the window; cayo installs no plymouth at all. Fix: a second bounded ExecStartPre 'udevadm wait /dev/fb0' as a console-handoff barrier -- the kernel prints 'Console: switching to colour frame buffer device' immediately before 'fb0: <drv>drmfb', so /dev/fb0 proves the takeover is done.
evidence: In-guest on both published candidates, same QEMU args as CI (test/lib/vm.sh, single virtio-gpu + -vga none): snow journal -k shows 'Console: switching to colour frame buffer device 160x50' at 4.948-5.020s with vtcon1 'frame buffer device' bind=1 and vtcon0 bind=0, virtio_gpu probe spanning 140ms; snowfield shows no console-switch line at all, vtcon0 dummy bind=1 only, probe spanning 21ms, and CONFIG_FRAMEBUFFER_CONSOLE_DEFERRED_TAKEOVER=y in /boot/config-6.19.8-surface-3 (absent from snow's 7.1.8+deb13-amd64). CI job 99732019952 journal: 'ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/udevadm wait /dev/dri/card0 (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS)' then 'Main PID: 687 (code=killed, signal=SEGV)' after 74ms.
promoted_to: docs/design/overview.md (Plymouth splash + Snow theme, mechanism 4); shared/snow/tree/usr/lib/systemd/system/plymouth-start.service.d/10-wait-drm.conf; test/native-ab-static-test.sh

scope: mkosi.images/{incus,dev}/, sysext delta composition vs. mkosi.images/base closure
correction: A published Overlay=yes sysext .raw is a frozen assertion about the BUILD BASE's transitive closure, and nothing revalidates it when base later shrinks. Removing network-manager-applet from base (33455fc, 2026-08-25, #771) -- which had been pulling an entire desktop through the policykit-1-gnome | polkit-1-auth-agent virtual -- retroactively broke the incus sysext published 2026-08-04: its delta had correctly omitted libgtk-3-0t64, libepoxy0, libgstreamer1.0-0, libopus0 and the rest of the GTK3/media closure as 'already in base', while still shipping qemu-system-gui, libsdl2-2.0-0, libvte-2.91-0, libgtk-vnc-2.0-0, libspice-client-gtk-3.0-5 and virt-viewer. skip-duplicates meant the unchanged KEYPACKAGE version never republished, so the stale delta stayed live. Two beliefs were wrong: (1) that adding a package to Packages= guarantees it reaches the delta -- omission is decided by PRESENCE IN BASE, not by how the package was requested, so only required-paths.txt (which checks the delta) can assert it; (2) that incus uses Debian's /usr/bin/qemu-system-x86_64 -- the incus deb bundles its own /usr/incus/bin/qemu-system-x86_64 and /usr/incus/lib/systemd/incusd prepends /usr/incus/bin to PATH, so the bundled binary is the one incusd probes, and Debian's working qemu is irrelevant. Blast radius is bounded exactly, not guessed: the set the old base supplied is (one pre-change sysext's post-change manifest) minus (its published .raw's package set), and intersecting that 88-package set with every other pre-change sysext's current manifest names the affected ones. For #771 that is incus (88 hits) and dev (81 hits) only; debdev, podman, nix, pilothouse, 1password-cli and tailscale also predate the change but intersect empty. paseo looked suspect from a narrow hand-picked lib scan but had already self-healed -- 0.7.0 was published 2026-08-31, after the base change -- which is also why per-sysext publish dates must be taken as the max Last-Modified over SHA256SUMS, never the first line: that file is not newest-first.
evidence: selfie (10.0.1.200, cayo-ab 20260901032038, incus sysext 1+7.3-debian13-202608040033+r1): 'incus launch --vm' -> 'Instance type "virtual-machine" is not supported on this server: Failed getting QEMU version'; incus info showed 'driver: lxc' only (snow showed 'lxc | qemu'). /usr/bin/qemu-system-x86_64 --version worked (Debian 10.0.11); /usr/incus/bin/qemu-system-x86_64 exited 127 with 'libepoxy.so.0: cannot open shared object file'. readelf -d on it lists libepoxy.so.0 in DT_NEEDED; libopus.so.0 is reached via libspice-server.so.1. An ldd sweep of /usr/bin,/usr/sbin,/usr/libexec plus the /usr/incus payload found 24 distinct unresolved sonames and flagged virt-viewer (35) and remote-viewer (34). systemd-dissect --list of the published .raw confirmed the delta contains libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-0 but not libgstreamer1.0-0, and qemu-system-gui/libsdl2/libvte but no libgtk-3-0t64 or libepoxy0. Snow (same sysext) was unaffected: GNOME supplies all of them; a VM created and started there successfully. Affected-set derivation: comm -23 of output/incus.manifest against the installed incus_1+7.3-debian13-202608040033+r1 raw's usr/share/doc entries = 88 packages (adwaita-icon-theme, libgtk-3-0t64, libepoxy0, libgstreamer1.0-0, libopus0, mesa-libgallium, ...); intersecting that with each other pre-2026-08-25 sysext's local manifest gave dev=81 and zero for the rest. Verified the fix needs no code change beyond a republish: a local build against the post-#771 base carries 174 packages vs the published 87, and systemd-dissect --list confirms all four newly pinned required paths.
promoted_to: AGENTS.md Sysext Constraints ('A published sysext delta is frozen against the base it was built on'); docs/design/sysexts.md 'A Sysext Delta Is Only Valid Against the Base It Was Built On' incl. the blast-radius procedure; mkosi.images/incus/{mkosi.conf SYSEXT_REVISION=2, required-paths.txt}; mkosi.images/dev/{mkosi.conf SYSEXT_REVISION=2, required-paths.txt}

scope: GdkPixbuf caches in base-built graphical sysexts
correction: The live Snow icon loss was not a missing librsvg2-common package and not an icon-theme.cache regression. Snow's manifest contained librsvg2-common, its SVG loader module existed, and hicolor correctly had no icon cache. The newly rebuilt dev r2 and incus r2 sysexts plus Paseo 0.7.0 each shipped a 2,582-byte /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gdk-pixbuf-2.0/2.10.0/loaders.cache generated from their recommends-off base-built GTK closure. Every cache omitted libpixbufloader_svg.so; the highest-precedence sysext copy shadowed Snow's complete base loader cache for all of merged /usr, so GNOME could not use the SVG module that was physically present.
evidence: Live Snow: /usr/share/frostyard/snow.packages.txt lists librsvg2-common 2.60.0+dfsg-1; dpkg-query -L shows libpixbufloader_svg.so; merged loaders.cache is 2582 bytes and has no SVG entry; journalctl _COMM=gnome-shell logs 'Could not load a pixbuf from icon theme'; dump.erofs --offset=1048576 showed the identical incomplete cache inside active dev_12.12+r2, incus_...+r2, and paseo_0.7.0 raw images. gdk-pixbuf-query-loaders over the merged module directory does register SVG, proving the module itself is valid.
promoted_to: AGENTS.md GdkPixbuf loader caches in sysexts; docs/design/sysexts.md Desktop Applications in Sysexts; shared/sysext/finalize/sysext-strip-icon-cache.sh; test/sysext-authoring-contract-test.sh
